narrative.overview:
Moving Curve is the independent single-author finance newsletter played straight, at the craft level of the Collaborative Fund blog and Net Interest. It does not wear a costume; it earns distinction through typographic precision. A serif reading face carries titles and body at a real measure; a workhorse sans carries everything that is apparatus (meta, navigation, tables, chart text, captions). Numbers are always tabular.

The page is white paper, near-black ink, hairline rules and one deep blue. That blue is both the link colour and the first chart series, so the reader learns one signal: blue is the author's line of argument, in prose and in data. Structure is drawn with rules, never with boxes: the feed is ruled rows, the model attachment is a ruled row, tables are ruled ledgers, the contents rail is a single left rule. Light and dark themes are the same system remapped through the same tokens.

Charts, pasted tables, captioned images and captioned Markdown tables are one family: numbered exhibits with a single caption style, a source line, and accessible data behind every chart. The confirmed rejection is the off-the-shelf blog theme: stock card grids, hero banners, Medium-style chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Serif for reading, sans for apparatus, tabular figures wherever a number appears.
One accent (ledger blue) shared by links and chart series 1.
Hairline rules instead of cards; flat surfaces; no shadows at rest.
Every chart, table and figure is a numbered "Exhibit N" in one shared sequence.
Light and dark from one token set, via `prefers-color-scheme`.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Ledger blue is the only accent in the interface. It marks links, the mark's dot, focus, and chart series 1; it never fills a surface or a button.

rules.name: The Validated Series Rule
rules.body: Chart slots are fixed and ordered (blue, copper, aqua, ochre, magenta). Slot 1 is always the link accent; slots 2-5 passed the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD and normal-vision delta E) in both schemes. Do not substitute hues, and do not use a neutral grey ramp for series: it was tested and failed the validator.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif is the author speaking (titles, deks, prose, quotes). Sans is the apparatus (meta, navigation, exhibits, tables, footnotes). Never set a chart label or table in serif, or a headline in sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can line up does: dates, meta, years, exhibit labels, ticks, values, tooltips and tables all use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, labels and captions are sentence case at normal tracking. Hierarchy comes from weight and size, never from uppercase tracking.

rules.name: The Ruled Page Rule
rules.body: No cards, no panels, no shadows. Group with a hairline above and below; separate with whitespace. The active nav underline and active topic underline are 1.5px ink rules drawn with an inset box-shadow, which is a rule, not elevation.

dos: Do set reading text in the serif at 1.1875rem/1.65 inside the 42.5rem measure.
Do set every number in tabular figures, and right-align numeric table columns.
Do separate content with 1px hairlines (`rule`) and reserve the ink rule for headers, totals and year dividers.
Do caption every chart, data table and figure as a numbered "Exhibit N" in the shared sequence, with a source line where the data has one.
Do use chart slots in their fixed order, with slot 1 equal to the link accent in each scheme.
Do give any chart with two or more series a legend, and add direct end labels on wide line charts only when they do not collide.
Do give every chart a text label and a "View data" table.
Do keep light and dark in step by changing tokens, never by adding per-theme components.
donts: Don't use cards, panels or tiles to group content; use a ruled row.
Don't add shadows; the transient chart tooltip is the only exception.
Don't introduce a second accent colour in the interface, or fill buttons or surfaces with ledger blue.
Don't replace the validated series hues or use a neutral grey ramp for chart series.
Don't add uppercase tracked labels, eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't set tables, chart labels or meta in the serif.
Don't reach for the off-the-shelf blog theme: stock card grids, hero banners, Medium-style chrome.
